name: Nigel Farage
role: Leader of Reform UK; MP for Clacton since 2024; former UKIP and Brexit Party leader and MEP (1999-2020)
summary: A right-populist, Eurosceptic politician whose platform centres on national sovereignty, sharply lower immigration, leaving the ECHR, scrapping Net Zero and tax cuts. He backs a free-at-the-point-of-use NHS with more competition and has occasionally supported state action, such as nationalising steel, alongside a tough law-and-order and anti-'woke' agenda. He is personally opposed to the death penalty and describes himself as pro-choice with a lower time limit.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Says the NHS 'will always be free at the point of delivery under a Reform government'; has also floated an insurance-style funding model but says he was misinterpreted and that care would stay free.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: 2024 Contract stresses backing 'risk takers and wealth creators', scrapping thousands of laws and 'nanny state regulations'; no direct statement of the principle found.

public-ownership.rationale: Called for 'immediate nationalisation' of the Scunthorpe steelworks and the 2024 Contract proposes 50% public ownership of each utility (50% pension funds), but he has not backed public ownership of energy, rail or utilities generally.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: 2024 Contract cuts corporation tax, entrepreneurs' tax and inheritance tax, and keeps the higher rate starting at 70,000 pounds; no push for higher taxes on the wealthy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Contract promises to scrap thousands of laws on business including employment laws and make hiring and firing easier, though it also gives the CMA powers on supermarket pricing.

cut-welfare.rationale: Contract calls the benefits system 'broken', targets 15bn pounds a year in benefit savings and says 'if you can work, you must work'; in 2025 he said he is not supporting a benefits culture but wants the two-child cap ended.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Contract's proposed Bill of Rights says surveillance of the public must be limited and those monitoring us held to account.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Contract: mandatory life imprisonment for drug dealing and trafficking and heavy fines for substantial possession.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Told the US Congress and promised to repeal the Online Safety Act and go back to pre-2010 law on how hate speech is interpreted; Contract redefines hate crime and proposes a Free Speech Bill.

state-harmful.rationale: Contract expands police, prisons, the armed forces and keeps a free NHS; he does not argue for abolishing the state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Contract: 40,000 more police, zero-tolerance policing and more stop and search, defence spending to 3% of GDP.

rehabilitation.rationale: Contract promises a justice system that 'punishes criminals', 'life means life' and 10,000 more prison places, with training camps for young offenders.

traditional-family.rationale: Contract: 'strong families are the bedrock of a thriving society'; backs transferable marriage allowance.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2025 said 'I didn't support it' and it was wrong to introduce without a manifesto commitment, but called it 'a settled issue' and 'we have moved on'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as pro-choice while saying the 24-week limit is 'utterly ludicrous' and should be reduced.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Contract scraps DE&I and 'positive action'; in 2026 said politicians had created a 'backdoor for anti-white discrimination'.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Contract calls 'transgender indoctrination' harmful to children and bans gender questioning in schools; no direct statement on gender as construct.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Foreword: 'Only Reform UK will stand up for British culture, identity and values'; St George's and St David's days as public holidays.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Foreword and core pledge: freeze non-essential immigration; 'Smart immigration, not mass immigration'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Contract rejects the WHO Pandemic Treaty and WEF influence and leaves the ECHR; has long campaigned against EU institutions.

nation-first.rationale: 'Take back control over our borders, our money and our laws'; reject WHO treaty and WEF; leave the ECHR.

open-borders.rationale: Pledges to freeze non-essential immigration, detain and deport illegal arrivals.

limit-growth.rationale: Contract is built around 'real economic growth' and says Britain must not impoverish itself in pursuit of CO2 targets.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Core pledge to 'scrap Net Zero'; in 2024 said 'I'm not arguing the science' but called Net Zero targets unaffordable and said UK emissions are a small share.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Contract: fast-track clean nuclear energy with small modular reactors built in Britain.

experts-over-public.rationale: Favours referendums and attacks the 'out-of-touch' elite; Contract would, however, replace civil service heads with private-sector professionals.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Contract abolishes inheritance tax on estates under 2m pounds and sets a 20% rate above that (with a charity option); he also backed farmers against inheritance tax changes.

direct-votes.rationale: Campaigned for the Brexit referendum, launched a campaign for a referendum on net zero and wants a referendum on proportional representation.

political-violence-never.rationale: Condemned the 2024 riots ('no place in a functioning democracy') and said he did not support violence; condemned milkshake attacks as undermining democracy.

conscription.rationale: Contract rejects one-year national service as 'not the answer', proposing 30,000 full-time army recruits instead.

national-self-determination.rationale: 'As a champion of national sovereignty' says Putin was wrong to invade the sovereign nation of Ukraine; 2016 wants Britain an 'independent, self-governing' nation.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Contract requires 5 years' residency and employment to claim any benefits, bars foreign nationals from social housing priority; ILR replacement is a visa without benefit access.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Contract: job seekers must find work within 4 months or accept a job after 2 offers or lose benefits; 'if you can work, you must work'.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Foreword and pledges: 'unlock Britain's vast energy treasure of oil and gas', fast-track North Sea licences, shale test sites, 'explore clean coal'.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Contract says multiculturalism has 'imported separate communities that reject our way of life' and pledges to defend British values; does not use the word assimilate.

proportional-representation.rationale: Contract: proportional representation for the Commons, subject to a referendum.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Foreword signed by Farage: 'out-of-touch political class'; Contract speaks of the 'corruption of government and politics by an out-of-touch, London-centric elite'; told MEPs none had 'done a proper job'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Contract keeps a tax-funded NHS free at the point of use, benefits system and public utility stakes rather than a minimal state.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Contract pledges to 'stop Sharia law being used in the UK'.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contract blames mass immigration and multiculturalism for separate communities and strain on public services.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contract proposes a Free Speech Bill and scrapping the TV licence; he campaigns against censorship and compared Starmer's government with North Korea.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Wants to abolish indefinite leave to remain, replacing it with a renewable five-year visa and requiring existing holders to reapply; no explicit citizenship-wait statement opened.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Career-long campaign to leave the EU; told MEPs the EU is an 'imposed' political union and the UK will not be the last to leave.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Contract keeps a lead role in NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: Says that given miscarriages of justice 'I don't think I could ever support it', calling it a conscience issue and not Reform policy.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Called the Online Safety Act's age checks on pornography sites 'massive overreach' and promised repeal, with a different child-protection approach.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Contract cuts foreign aid by 50% (6bn pounds).

collective-defense.rationale: Contract commits to 'our lead role in NATO' and raising defence spending.

equal-parenting.rationale: Contract: share parental care 50/50 'where appropriate' and give grandparents access rights.

common-currency.rationale: Told MEPs in 2016 they were 'in denial' that their currency is failing; Contract: take back control of 'our money'.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wants to curb foreign and judge-made rights law and put Parliament first, but also proposes a codified Bill of Rights protecting freedoms.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Contract scraps DE&I rules and replaces the Equalities Act, whose 'positive action' he says requires discrimination.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Contract replaces the 'crony-filled' House of Lords with an elected smaller chamber; hereditary titles are not mentioned.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Contract: 'Our children must be taught about their heritage'; imperialism teaching to be paired with non-European examples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Contract: a 'patriotic curriculum' so pupils are 'proud of Britain'.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Contract scraps DE&I rules and the 2010 Equalities Act's 'positive action'; 2026: schools should not be forced to celebrate Black History Month.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Contract proposes a British Bill of Rights in which 'our freedoms must be codified and guaranteed'; entrenchment is not specified.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Argued that leaving the ECHR would 'restore the power of this Parliament'; says the UK is 'not sovereign' while subject to a foreign court.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Contract front-loads child benefit for ages 1-4 and backs marriage tax allowance, while cutting immigration; no explicit birth-rate aim.

national-law-over-international.rationale: 'We are not sovereign all the while we are part of the ECHR'; wants to leave the ECHR and disapply the Refugee Convention and other treaties for five years.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Wants competing insurers/independent providers delivering care from the existing national insurance money, plus an NHS voucher scheme and use of independent capacity, with care free at the point of use.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Contract bans 'transgender ideology' in schools and mandates single-sex spaces and replaces the Equalities Act.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Contract adds police and prison places.

second-chamber.rationale: Contract replaces the Lords with 'a much smaller, more democratic second chamber'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Contract raises defence spending to 2.5% then 3% of GDP.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Contract scraps interest on student loans and extends repayment to 45 years; it does not cancel debts.

public-service-media.rationale: Contract calls the BBC institutionally biased and scraps the TV licence.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Contract pledges to ban ULEZ, low traffic neighbourhoods and petrol/diesel bans ('stop the war on drivers').

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Contract: mandatory life for a second violent or serious offence and for drug trafficking.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: No opened source records a language requirement from him.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Contract scraps VAT on energy bills, abolishes the VAT 'tourist tax' and lifts the VAT threshold to 150,000 pounds.

national-resource-control.rationale: Contract seeks national control of UK waters (licence fees for foreign vessels, fisheries patrol) and exploitation of North Sea oil and gas for Britain.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Says 'Reform is now the party of the workers' while campaigning on national identity and sovereignty.

notes: Party-programme answers rely on the 2024 Contract, whose foreword Farage signed and which he launched; later 2025 announcements (Operation Restoring Justice, ILR abolition) were read through press and scholarly accounts. Views changed on NHS funding (insurance model floated 2012-2025, then 'always free at the point of delivery') and climate (2024 shift from party climate denial to 'not arguing the science'). Unreachable: Hansard and TheyWorkForYou (403/503), europarl.europa.eu not tried, Express & Star, SCMP, Deccan Herald, Pravda (403), his books (no full text). Assisted dying vote, water nationalisation and Islam-specific claims were found only in unopened search summaries and are left null.
